approval.cost: No Go-Live or review fee is stated in the docs read; envelope-send pricing follows the classification and your production plan ('To understand the specific pricing for each send type, review your Docusign production plan details or contact your Docusign representative')
approval.trigger: The Go-Live process is the gate: an integration key works only in the developer (demo) environment until it is promoted, and promotion enables 'Sending of legally binding eSignature requests' and 'Any user on any production Docusign account to access your app'. Prerequisites (verbatim): 'OAuth 2.0 authentication configured for your app'; 'A paid production account that will serve as the management account for the app in the production environment. ISV partners can apply for a free IK management account via the partner program'; and 'Administrator access or developer access to the production account'. Step 1 is a classification choice, which 'also affects how envelopes are billed on your production account': Private custom integration (your/your customers' employees); Third-party integration key (a partner integration that requires you to supply your own IK); Public integration ('You're building a public integration for multiple Docusign customers, who will access it using their own Docusign accounts... You'll need to join the Docusign Partner Program to launch a public integration'); or Embedded integration ('you'll need to be an ISV Embed partner, which requires a special license'). Then one of two paths: (a) Automatic promotion: 'Your integration may be eligible for automatic promotion to production without a Docusign review', ending in status 'App is live'; a 'Declined / Verification required' status appears if 'a one-time identity verification process must be completed for the production account', after which you retry. (b) Go-Live review: status changes to 'Pending approval'; 'After the app has passed review, you will receive an email notification and the key's status changes to App is live. If your app fails the review, its status changes to Declined.' Pre-approval cap: the key is confined to the demo environment; no production users can connect at all.
approval.wait: Not stated (no duration in the current Go-Live documentation; a Docusign community announcement about the streamlined Apps & Keys Go-Live experience says it eliminates the historical 20-API-calls requirement and that 'in most cases' an eligible integration 'can go live instantly', but that is a community announcement, not the developer docs)

blockers.detail: 'When your app is promoted into the production environment, its integration key is duplicated into the production environment rather than moved. The integration key's configuration parameters such as secrets and redirect URIs are not also duplicated; you must add them in the production environment.' The key keeps the same GUID and keeps working in demo. And: 'Can I use the same integration key, client secret, or RSA key pair in Demo and Production? No. Demo and Production are separate environments... you must generate new client secrets and RSA key pairs for Production.'
blockers.howToClear: Budget a full production re-configuration step (redirect URIs, new secrets/keypairs, production endpoints) into the launch plan.
blockers.title: Promotion duplicates the key; configuration does not follow

blockers.detail: The standard refresh token dies 30 days after the original grant regardless of use, unless you requested the extended scope, which makes each refresh mint a new 30-day refresh token. It can also die early: 'A refresh token can also become invalid before its expiration date if the user changes their password or revokes application consent.'
blockers.howToClear: Request the extended scope at consent time if connections must outlive 30 days.
blockers.title: Refresh-token clock is anchored to the initial consent

blockers.detail: 'OAuth access tokens cannot be directly revoked. Revoking application consent prevents new tokens from being generated but does not invalidate existing tokens': an issued token lives out its 8 hours (or 1 hour for JWT).
blockers.howToClear: Design with the 8-hour exposure window in mind; there is no kill switch for a leaked access token.
blockers.title: Access tokens cannot be revoked

alternatives: Public Authorization Code Grant (same flow without a secret, using PKCE, S256 only; for SPAs/native apps that 'cannot secure a secret key'; Docusign says it 'should be used instead of the Implicit Grant for all use cases')

JWT Grant (a service integration model: your app signs a JWT with its RSA private key to impersonate one specific user, requiring the signature + impersonation scopes and prior consent; fits system/admin-login backends, not per-user connect flows; grants NO refresh token and tokens last 1 hour)
Implicit Grant (legacy; official docs steer you to Public ACG instead)
flavor.recommended: Confidential Authorization Code Grant on an App and Integration Key
flavor.why: The object is an App and Integration Key, created in Apps and Keys in the developer (demo) account's Docusign Admin. The Integration Key is the OAuth client_id (a GUID); you add a Secret Key (the client_secret) for Authorization Code Grant, and/or an RSA keypair for JWT Grant. Per the official Authorization Code Grant page, use the confidential flavor when 'Your users have Docusign accounts and log in to your integrated application individually' and 'Your integration is hosted on a server'. It provides an 8-hour access token plus a refresh token, with optional PKCE. There is no API-key auth for the eSignature API; OAuth 2.0 is the only model ('Your REST integration must use OAuth 2.0, or you must request a policy exception').

humanMust: Add the App / Integration Key in Apps and Keys; configure Authorization Code Grant, redirect URIs, and generate the Secret Key (copy it immediately)
Complete Go-Live: classification, then automatic promotion or review; a paid production account serves as the management account (public integrations also require the Docusign Partner Program)
Re-configure the key in production: add redirect URIs and generate NEW secret keys / RSA keypairs in the production account, and switch endpoints to account.docusign.com
name: DocuSign
nuances: 'A promoted key cannot be deleted from production', only disabled by removing its secret key and RSA key pair in Apps and Keys (it can be re-enabled later). Per-user data-center routing: the production API base URI differs per account ({server} such as CA, NA2, EU), discoverable from /oauth/userinfo; a multi-tenant SaaS must store it per connected account.
'An access token's lifetime cannot be extended.' Redirect URIs must match exactly, 'including space and slash characters', a common failure.

JWT consent is the main JWT failure mode (consent_required): an integration may need to support individual consent AND admin consent (internal and external variants), and admin consent for an external application may require an entitlement (organizations lacking it must open a support case, per the support FAQ). Sharing an RSA private key with a third-party vendor has security implications; Docusign's FAQ advises asking such vendors to use Authorization Code Grant instead.

Review data expiry: 'A key in this status had previously undergone review but was not submitted by selecting Actions > Start Go Live. Unless submitted for processing, the review data only persists for a limited amount of time' (duration not quantified).
prerequisites: A paid production account to serve as the management account (or an ISV free IK management account via the partner program)
Administrator or developer access to the production account

steps.detail: Create the developer account, then Apps and Keys > Add App / Integration Key; name the app and note the Integration Key (the OAuth client_id).
steps.title: Create a developer account; add the app

steps.detail: Set the authentication type to Authorization Code Grant, add your Redirect URI(s), and generate a Secret Key (copy it immediately). For JWT instead, generate an RSA keypair and note the target user's API Username (GUID).
steps.title: Configure the app

steps.detail: Send the user to account-d.docusign.com/oauth/auth (demo: account-d.docusign.com) with response_type=code, scope=signature (space-separated scopes), client_id=<integration key>, redirect_uri=<uri>. The user logs in and grants consent. Exchange the returned code (2-minute lifetime) at /oauth/token using HTTP Basic auth (Integration Key : Secret Key).

links.label: Get an access token with Confidential Authorization Code Grant

steps.title: Run the flow; exchange the code

steps.detail: Call /oauth/userinfo to get the user's account_id and base_uri (their production data center, e.g. NA2/EU/CA) and cache it; all API calls go to that base URI with Authorization: Bearer. Refresh with the refresh token before the 8-hour access token expires (standard refresh token: 30 days from the initial consent grant; extended scope makes refreshes roll).
steps.title: Resolve the data center; call the API; refresh

steps.detail: In the demo account, start Go-Live: choose the classification (public integrations require joining the Docusign Partner Program), then automatic promotion if eligible (or 'Verification required' identity verification, or 'Pending approval' review). On success the status becomes 'App is live'.
steps.title: Complete Go-Live

steps.detail: Add redirect URIs and generate new secret keys / RSA keypairs in the production account, and switch endpoints to account.docusign.com and https://{server}.docusign.net/restapi/v2.1/.
steps.title: Re-configure the key in production

tagline: An Integration Key promoted from demo to production through Go-Live: Confidential Authorization Code Grant (8-hour tokens, 2-minute codes, refresh tokens anchored to the initial consent), a classification choice that can require the Partner Program, and a production environment where nothing, not even your secrets, carries over.
